# AI Wise

> AI Wise is the one-person practice of Simon van Meegdenburg. Using AI, he
> builds apps, websites and tools that take recurring work off people's hands,
> preferably for small practices and organizations doing meaningful work.
> Tagline: Automation in Service of Life.

The website is a single page in Dutch and English. It describes what has become
possible, gives examples, introduces Simon and explains how to get in touch. It
deliberately carries no service catalogue, no pricing and no productised offer.

## What has changed

Having a website, an app or a tool built has become considerably more
accessible. With AI, the path from a clear idea to something that works is much
shorter, and what used to be a large project is now manageable. That makes it
feasible for small practices and organizations too. AI is the method here, not
the subject.

## Examples

The website gives these as examples of what is possible, to think with. They
are not a service catalogue.

- A renewed website.
- A webshop alongside a practice.
- An online learning environment alongside in-person classes.
- Registrations that land directly in the administration.
- Participants who manage their own registrations or membership.
- Meeting notes that write themselves up.
- A tool for the one recurring task that takes too much time.

## What the website does not include

- No pricing, packages or scope.
- No case studies, client names or testimonials, because none are confirmed for
  public use.
- No claims about time saved, safety or privacy outcomes.

## Contact

The site invites two kinds of message, and treats both as equally welcome: an
organization orienting itself on what AI could mean for its work, and a fellow
developer building with AI who wants to compare notes. Contact runs by email at
simon@aiwise.it.com or by WhatsApp on +31 6 13926494. There is no contact form.

## Crawling

Regular search crawlers, AI search and discovery crawlers, and user-triggered
fetchers are welcome to read and cite this site. Model-training crawlers are
disallowed in robots.txt; that is a deliberate and separate choice from being
findable in AI-assisted search.
